theme: Arthurian court: a crown and a shield passed between knight, fairy, queen and king
hint: The same little word can mean “the” or something else. Look at where it stands: before a noun, or before the verb?

corpus.lang: Le roi donne la couronne au chevalier.
corpus.en: The king gives the crown to the knight.

corpus.lang: Le chevalier la donne à la fée.
corpus.en: The knight gives it to the fairy.

corpus.lang: La fée lui montre le bouclier.
corpus.en: The fairy shows him the shield.

corpus.lang: Le dragon ne voit pas les chevaliers.
corpus.en: The dragon does not see the knights.

corpus.lang: Le dragon ne les voit pas.
corpus.en: The dragon does not see them.
The queen shows it to them.

corpus.lang: Le roi ne leur donne pas le bouclier.
corpus.en: The king does not give them the shield.
The fairy gives them to her.

corpus.lang: Le chevalier ne la leur montre pas.
corpus.en: The knight does not show it to them.

accepted: the dragon gives it to them
the dragon is giving it to them
the dragon is giving them it
the dragon gives him to them
the dragon is giving him to them
toEnglish.explanation: The first le is “the” (it sits before a noun); the second le sits before the verb, so it is the pronoun “it”. leur is “to them”.

toLang.prompt: The queen does not show them to him.
accepted: La reine ne les lui montre pas.
toLang.explanation: Both pronouns go before the verb, “it/them” first, then “to him/her/them”, and ne … pas wraps around the whole block.

grammar: Object pronouns come before the verb, not after it.
When there are two, the direct object comes first.
Negation wraps around the pronouns and the verb together.
explain.notes: French has no separate word for “it”: a thing is le or la depending on the gender of the noun it replaces (la for la couronne, le for le bouclier). lui does not mark gender at all: it is “to him” in one sentence and “to her” in another.
explain.fact: French nouns lost their Latin case endings centuries ago, but the pronouns kept a trace of them: le and lui both come from Latin ille “that”, and lui continues a Late Latin dative form, illui.
